label: 2026-11-21-outcome
notes: Pilot: one repetition, 11 paired tasks (n = 11). The 95 % intervals are wide; read the differences as direction and rough size, not as a precise estimate.

Budget: --max-turns 4, i.e. at most three rounds of tool calls before the final answer (parallel calls in one reply share a round; checked with probe against the mock API). The prompt states this in both conditions. Every failed none session reached the limit with a fourth round of tool calls and so ended without an answer (status max_turns, F1 = 0); no session in either condition ended with a wrong answer below the threshold.

Calibration (10 sessions, condition none, the same prompt): 5 of 6 tasks succeeded at --max-turns 8 (results/2026-11-21-outcome-calibration, at the ceiling; that prompt still said parallel calls count one turn each, which the probe disproved), 1 of 4 at --max-turns 4 (results/2026-11-21-outcome-calibration-t4). The main run uses 4.

Session accounting: 23 of the 24 approved sessions launched, 22 graded. django-amb-transaction-get-connection (C) was killed with its run chunk by an external stop after its first tool call and was run again; django-tc-resolve-url was therefore not run in either condition, because its pair would have exceeded the budget.

Index: the django/ package (12,443 symbols, all 12,443 embedded with the default jina-embeddings-v2-base-code, template 2, chunking), built once with myc analyze --strict-embeddings (1,447 s, 1,324 s of it embedding) and copied fresh for every C session. The probe showed the SessionStart hook reporting it ready (index commit = HEAD), so no session re-indexed.

The gold sets follow static call rules (calls by name, self/cls/super() through the enclosing class and its bases, instantiation by name) that the question spells out. A call graph computes exactly this by construction, while an agent with grep has to emulate it; the tasks were chosen by graph properties (depth, files, same-named functions) before any myceliums output was seen, but they are structural questions of the kind myceliums is built for.

Success as an exact sign (McNemar) test: 7 tasks are discordant, all 7 failed in none and succeeded in C, none the other way; two-sided p = 2 x 0.5^7 = 0.016. It agrees with the bootstrap interval above (+36 to +91 pp).

The budget was chosen in calibration because the agent without myceliums failed at it (3 of 4 calibration tasks at --max-turns 4, all three also in this run); the calibration covered 9 of the 12 tasks. With up to seven rounds (and the earlier, partly wrong budget text) it had solved 5 of 6. Only the success gain is therefore shown to be a budget effect; C never ran without a budget.

The cost, token and wall-time ratios hold under this budget only: the failed none sessions were cut off at the turn limit, which also caps their cost and time. Without a budget these were not measured, apart from the four blast-radius tasks both conditions solved (C 2.25 vs 4.25 tool calls, 12.5 vs 21.8 s, 0.047 vs 0.069 USD; n = 4, descriptive).
Neither condition had a shell: the built-in tools were Read, Grep and Glob (the harness also allows ToolSearch, which the CLI drops when no MCP server is configured).

Tasks frozen before any myceliums output: tasks/tasks-outcome.json (sha256 3a1b3848ce66bb2612cdf2c39d27fa8688280189bce55d07e782719a637767d6, the tasks_sha256 above and in both calibration directories) was committed in 9619d24 at 2026-11-21T20:56:11Z and has not changed since; the questions in all 32 graded prompts, from the first calibration session (20:47:13Z), are the committed ones. The Django index finished at 20:59:17Z (indexed_at); the first session with myceliums (a mock-API probe) started at 20:59:41Z, this run at 21:00:18Z. Before, myc had only counted symbols (a graph-only analyze and myc stats), never listed callers.
